proposition.claim:
The convergence theorem assumes some deterministic \(\lambda>0\) lower-bounds every empirical Hessian almost surely.

Total expert weight above \(D/2\) alone is not sufficient when singular precisions are allowed; the paper explicitly notes and checks this limitation.

repair.content: A conditional mean-contraction premise \(E[(1+\eta m_t)^{-1}\mid\mathcal F_t]\le\rho<1\), with \(m_t=\lambda_{\min}(M_t)\), yields \(E\|e_t\|\le\rho^t\|e_0\|+\eta\delta(1-\rho^t)/(1-\rho)\) from the quadratic variational inequality. This is a different assumption; its multivariate applicability is unestablished.
